title: The all-British album The Song of the Tenor
summary: Phonogram asked Freeman for an album and he used British players such as Bruce Turner, Roy Williams and Bob Wilber's arrangements.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: Oh, very much so. We made an album called The Song of the Tenor and Bruce is on that. The recording company Phonogram asked me if I'd like to do an album and what would I like to use, and I said, I would like to do an all British album, use all British musicians who are exploited too much, and Bob Wilber happened to be here and so we used Bob and it was a fine album, with Bruce, Bob and I on reeds, and a young London pianist by the name of Keith Ingam, plays very well, and he's going to the States by the way, to play, to work, to live, and a fine bass player by the name of -- oh, dear, I'm that way about names again. A drummer by the name of Bobby Orr -- well, as I mentioned Bruce Turner, oh, yes, Roy Williams, who is a very fine trombone player. George Wein used about six British musicians in the Nice festival just last July and they were a big success.
Roy Williams, I don't know all the men, who were on it, but I know they used just six British musicians.
That's very nice, isn't it. Well, who did arrangements on that session or did you use arrangements.
Well, I wasn't on the Nice festival this year.
No, I don't mean that, I mean on the album.
Oh, yes, Bob Wilber wrote out some very nice things.
